title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens Chapter VI, 'The general groups M_{rho,sigma}: recapitulation, refinement', of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'.

Setting, recalled from V.1 (p. 577):
- 𝔊 is a profinite group with a surjection GL(2,Z)^ -> 𝔊. Equivalently, 𝔊 has topological generators rho, sigma, tau (or rho, sigma, tau'), images of the standard elliptic and reflection generators of GL(2,Z).
- 𝔊^+ is the index-<=2 'orientation-preserving' part, the image of SL(2,Z)^.
- M (more generally M_{rho,sigma}) is the group of automorphisms of the data satisfying the 'loop equation'. This is Grothendieck's GT-type group.
- Gamma_Q^~ = M/𝔊^+ is the candidate combinatorial replacement for Gal(Qbar/Q), M modulo the inner part coming from 𝔊^+.

New datum: an open subgroup 𝔊^q_0 ⊂ 𝔊^+, normal in 𝔊^+.
- In the universal case 𝔊 = GL(2,Z)^, he defines M^q = {u in M : u normalises 𝔊^q and acts trivially on the finite group 𝔊^+/𝔊^q}.
- This contains 𝔊^+ (inner automorphisms act trivially on the abelianised quotient? not automatically, but on 𝔊^+/𝔊^q by conjugation). He therefore implicitly needs that 𝔊^+ acts trivially, or else M^q is meant together with the image. The image Gamma_Q^{q~} of M^q in Gamma_Q^~ is open.
- Modern reading: this is the GT-analogue of Gal(Qbar/K_q), where K_q is the field of moduli/definition of the finite étale cover of the moduli stack M_{1,1} (or of P^1 minus 3 points) corresponding to 𝔊^q, with its Galois group acting trivially.
- He proposes to study representations of these open subgroups Gamma_Q^{q~} into suitable profinite groups, the analogue of the Galois representations cut out by level structures.

Special cases:
- 𝔊^q = Pi_0 gives M^q = M^{!!}.
- 𝔊^q = Pi (the free profinite group on two generators, pi_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,inf}, i.e. the Gamma(2)-type subgroup) gives M^q = M^!.
- 𝔊^q = 𝔊 gives M^q = M, recovering the earlier constructions.

The next page adds 𝔊 = integral adelic points of a Z-group scheme, e.g. GL2(Zhat) congruence quotients, where rho, sigma, tau generate only an open subgroup. It suggests taking 𝔊^q inside the neutral component, and defines 𝔊^q_tau = {1,tau}·𝔊^q.

Purpose: to refine the GT-type group by level structures, getting open subgroups of Gamma_Q^~ and the corresponding 'relative' groups M^q_{rho,sigma}.
errors: Notation drifts between 𝔊^q_0 and 𝔊^q. The definition of M^q, after the crossed-out rewrite, leaves implicit why 𝔊^+ ⊂ M^q. Elements of 𝔊^+ act on 𝔊^+/𝔊^q by conjugation, not trivially in general unless the quotient is abelian. So either M^q must be taken as generated with 𝔊^+, or the image in Gamma_Q^~ must be defined via the action modulo inner automorphisms of 𝔊^+/𝔊^q. Minor gap.

ideas.what: Open subgroups of the GT-type group Gamma_Q^~ = M/𝔊^+ cut out by an open normal subgroup 𝔊^q of the profinite (S)L2-type group: elements acting trivially on 𝔊^+/𝔊^q.
ideas.modern_name: Stabilisers in GT of finite étale covers of M_{1,1} / P^1-{0,1,inf}; GT-analogues of Gal(Qbar/K) for fields of moduli of dessins (level structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura (GT action on SL2(Z)^); work on GT actions on dessins (Schneps, Guillot and others)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Galois action on dessins and on SL2(Z)^ but not this M^q formalism

ideas.what: Special cases 𝔊^q = Pi (free profinite on 2 generators) and Pi_0, giving M^! and M^!!, and recovering M when 𝔊^q = 𝔊.
ideas.modern_name: Passage between the GT action on pi_1(M_{1,1}) and on pi_1(P^1-3 points) (level 2 / Legendre family)

ideas.what: Proposal (next page) to take 𝔊 = integral adelic points of a Z-group scheme, with rho, sigma, tau generating only an open subgroup.
ideas.modern_name: Congruence quotients GL2(Zhat); arithmetic (adelic) target for GT-type actions

missed.claim: The program of studying representations of the level-cut open subgroups Gamma_Q^{q~} of the GT-type group into 'suitable profinite groups', as GT-analogues of Galois representations attached to level structures, is only announced here.
missed.quote: dont on pourra se proposer d'étudier les représentations dans des groupes profinis convenables
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: GT-versions of Galois representations of fields of moduli of dessins/modular covers are only partially developed in the literature. This is a mild unfinished thread, but close to known lines of work.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a set-up/recapitulation page introducing a level-subgroup refinement of Grothendieck's GT-type group. The idea is natural and closely parallels known work on GT acting on covers and dessins. Only the announced representation programme and the adelic group-scheme variant are slightly distinctive.
transcription_corrections: In (1) the subgroup is written 𝔊^q_0 with subscript 0; later occurrences drop the 0.
The universal case reads 𝔊 = Gl(2,Z)^ (with hat), and the overlined '(profini)' is an insertion above 𝔊.
